# check_consecutive

## Description

Verifies whether time values in a dataset are consecutive based on the detected time interval (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly, yearly). If a `unit` column is specified, the check is performed within each unit.

```r
check_consecutive(data, time, unit = NULL, strict = FALSE, area = NULL)
```

## Arguments

- `data`: A data frame containing the dataset. Must include the time variable and optionally a unit variable.
- `time`: A string representing the name of the column in `data` that contains time values. The column should be in "yyyy-mm-dd" format or any format recognizable by `as.Date()`.
- `unit`: (Optional) A single character representing the name of the columns in `data` that identifies the different unit for which a time series is available, typically a spatial unit. If provided, the check will be performed separately within each unit.
- `strict`: If FALSE (default) return a warning, if TRUE return an error.
- `area`: Deprecated, use `unit` instead.

## Details

Different time intervals per unit are not allowed.

## Returns

If strict = FALSE, returns a logical value: `TRUE` if all time values are consecutive, and `FALSE` otherwise. If `strict = TRUE`, the function throws an error if the check is not met.

## Examples

```r
df <- data.frame(
  date = seq(as.Date("2020-01-01"), by = "day", length.out = 10),
  cases = 1:10
)
check_consecutive(df, time = "date")
```
